malisper/pgrust

Postgres rewritten in Rust, now faster than Postgres and Clickhouse

Language: Rust

Stars: 5,852

Forks: 232

Stars today: 27 stars today

README

<h1 align="center">pgrust</h1>

<p align="center">
  <strong>A Rust rewrite of Postgres.</strong>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <img alt="Postgres 18.6" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/Postgres-18.6-336791">
  <img alt="Version: v0.4-beta" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/version-v0.4--beta-blue">
  <a href="LICENSE"><img alt="License: AGPL-3.0" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blue"></a>
</p>

<div align="center">
  <a href="https://pgrust.com"><strong>Try pgrust in your browser →</strong></a>
  <span>  |  </span>
  <a href="https://discord.gg/FZZ4dbdvwU">Discord</a>
  <span>  |  </span>
  <a href="https://pgrust.com/#updates">Updates</a>
  <span>  |  </span>
  <a href="https://github.com/malisper/pgrust/issues">Issues</a>
</div>

<br />

> **New:** [Video of Michael's talk at PlanetScale on pgrust](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7L_nG3EBjck) — and the [slides](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_wDk4HPE9-MuiPBo_X-QdJUmFtVV0p8p/view).
>
> [How AI Changes the Economics of JIT Compilers](https://malisper.me/how-ai-changes-the-economics-of-jit-compilers/)
>
> **v0.4-beta is out:** [the release post](https://pgrust.com/blog/pgrust-v0-4-beta/) and [what's new](#whats-new-in-v04-beta).

pgrust is a re-implementation of Postgres meant to show what Postgres would
look like if it was built in 2026. It is wire compatible and even SQL dialect
compatible with Postgres.

Every line is Rust, written to match the behavior of the C implementation.
Rust makes it easy to re-architect several core Postgres pieces. pgrust has:

- Gravity, a new vectorized push-based, JIT compiled query engine
- A thread based concurrency model
- A query scheduler designed to keep any individual query from taking down
  your database
- An automatic memory manager: one memory budget, sized from the machine,
  covers the buffer pool, the columnar caches and running queries, and gives
  pgrust control of what happens when you're running low on memory, greatly
  reducing the chance of your whole DB being taken down by the OS OOM killer

and many other really awesome pieces. The scheduler and the memory manager go
after two of
[the four horsemen behind thousands of Postgres outages](https://malisper.me/the-four-horsemen-behind-thousands-of-postgres-outages/).

## Quickstart

**In your browser:** <https://pgrust.com>, a full pgrust server compiled to
WebAssembly, no install.

**On your machine:** download a release tarball from
<https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/>. Each one is self-contained: it
carries pgrust's own `bin/postgres`, `bin/initdb` and `bin/psql` plus the
share files they read, so you do not need a PostgreSQL install. The Linux
binaries need glibc 2.34 or newer (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL/Rocky 9 and
later); the macOS binaries need macOS 11 or newer.

| Tarball | Runs on |
|---|---|
| [`pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-x86_64.tar.gz) | any x86-64 CPU |
| [`pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-aarch64.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-aarch64.tar.gz) | any 64-bit Arm CPU |
| [`pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-x86_64-znver3.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-x86_64-znver3.tar.gz) | tuned for AMD Zen 3 and newer |
| [`pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-aarch64-neoverse-v2.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-aarch64-neoverse-v2.tar.gz) | tuned for Neoverse-V2 (AWS Graviton4, NVIDIA Grace) |
| [`pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-arm64.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-arm64.tar.gz) | macOS on Apple Silicon |
| [`pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-x86_64.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-x86_64.tar.gz) | macOS on Intel |
| [`pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-universal.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-universal.tar.gz) | macOS, either (both architectures in one binary) |

The Linux builds are profile-guided optimized. The tuned builds use
instructions only those CPUs (and newer ones) have; when in doubt, take the
generic build. Every tarball has a `.sha256` file next to it, and
[`MANIFEST.txt`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/MANIFEST.txt) lists
them all.

### Linux

```bash
# Pick your build: linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, linux-x86_64-znver3 or
# linux-aarch64-neoverse-v2 (see the table above).
PLATFORM=linux-x86_64

# Download pgrust, verify the checksum and unpack it.
curl -LO "https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz"
curl -LO "https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256"
sha256sum -c "pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256"
tar xzf "pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz"
cd pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-*/

# Create a data directory with pgrust's initdb.
bin/initdb -D /tmp/pgrust-data --no-locale --encoding UTF8 -U postgres

# Start the server. It runs in the foreground and logs to this terminal.
ulimit -s 65520
RUST_MIN_STACK=33554432 bin/postgres \
  -D /tmp/pgrust-data \
  -k /tmp -p 5432 \
  -c listen_addresses= \
  -c io_method=sync \
  -c max_stack_depth=60000
```

Leave the server running and connect from a second terminal, in the same
directory:

```bash
bin/psql -h /tmp -p 5432 -U postgres -c "select version()"
```

You should see `PostgreSQL 18.6 (pgrust 0.4-beta, build <commit>) on ...`,
where `<commit>` is the short commit the binary was built from.
`bin/postgres --version` prints `pgrust 0.4-beta (PostgreSQL 18.6 compatible)`.

### Docker

The prebuilt image on Docker Hub,
[`malisper/pgrust`](https://hub.docker.com/r/malisper/pgrust), is a drop-in
replacement for the official `postgres` image: same env vars
(`POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_DB`, `PGDATA`, ...), same
`/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` init scripts, same data volume at
`/var/lib/postgresql/data`. It carries the same `postgres` and `initdb`
binaries as the Linux release tarballs above, and initializes the cluster with
pgrust's own `initdb`; the only C PostgreSQL component in the image is `psql`
for the init scripts. `malisper/pgrust:v0.4-beta` is multi-arch (amd64 +
arm64); `v0.4-beta-amd64` and `v0.4-beta-arm64` pin one architecture.

```bash
docker run -d --name pgrust -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret -p 5432:5432 malisper/pgrust:v0.4-beta
```

Then connect, with your own `psql` or the one in the image:

```bash
psql -h localhost -p 5432 -U postgres
docker exec -it pgrust psql -U postgres
```

`malisper/pgrust:latest` still points at v0.3; use the `v0.4-beta` tag to get
this release. A data volume written by v0.3 holding columnar tables needs the
dump and restore described under
[Stopping, restarting, cleaning up](#stopping-restarting-cleaning-up).

### macOS

```bash
# Pick your build: macos-arm64 (Apple Silicon), macos-x86_64 (Intel) or
# macos-universal (both).
PLATFORM=macos-arm64

# Download pgrust, verify the checksum and unpack it. Download with curl: curl
# does not set the quarantine flag a browser download gets, so Gatekeeper stays
# out of the way (see the note below).
curl -LO "https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz"
curl -LO "https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256"
shasum -a 256 -c "pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256"
tar xzf "pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz"
cd "pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM"

# Create a data directory with pgrust's initdb.
bin/initdb -D /tmp/pgrust-data --no-locale --encoding UTF8 -U postgres

# Start the server. It runs in the foreground and logs to this terminal.
ulimit -s 65520
RUST_MIN_STACK=33554432 bin/postgres \
  -D /tmp/pgrust-data \
  -k /tmp -p 5432 \
  -c listen_addresses= \
  -c io_method=sync \
  -c max_stack_depth=60000
```

Leave the server running and connect from a second terminal, in the same
directory:

```bash
bin/psql -h /tmp -p 5432 -U postgres -c "select version()"
```

**A note on Gatekeeper:** the macOS binaries are signed ad hoc, not notarized
by Apple. Downloaded with curl as above, they are never quarantined and none
of this comes up. If you download with a browser instead, macOS refuses to run
them with "Apple could not verify ... is free of malware". Clear the flag with
`xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM`, or approve each
binary under System Settings > Privacy & Security > "Open Anyway".

### Columnar tables

Columnar storage (`pgrcolumnar`) is a table access method. Register it once in
each database, then create tables with `USING pgrcolumnar`:

```sql
CREATE ACCESS METHOD pgrcolumnar TYPE TABLE HANDLER heap_tableam_handler;

CREATE TABLE events (id bigint, kind text, val double precision, at timestamp)
  USING pgrcolumnar;
```

### Stopping, restarting, cleaning up

- **Stop the server** with Ctrl-C in its terminal, or `kill -INT <pid>`. That
  is Postgres' fast shutdown and it is safe.
- **Start it again** by rerunning the same server command with the same data
  directory. Your data is preserved across restarts.
- **Start over** by deleting the data directory: `rm -rf /tmp/pgrust-data`.
  This deletes all data in it.
- **If startup fails with** `FATAL: lock file "/tmp/.s.PGSQL.5432.lock"
  already exists`, another server, most likely an existing Postgres install,
  is already using port 5432. Start pgrust on a different port with `-p 5433`
  and connect with `psql -h /tmp -p 5433 -U postgres`. Whenever a regular
  Postgres is running on the same machine, check `select version()` after
  connecting; it is easy to silently connect to the wrong server and wonder
  why nothing behaves like pgrust.
- **If startup fails with** `could not open directory
  "/usr/local/pgsql/share/timezone"`, the server cannot find its share files.
  It reads them from the `share` directory beside the binary, so run
  `bin/postgres` from the unpacked tarball as is, without moving the binary
  away from `bin/share`. `PGRUST_PGSHAREDIR` and `PGRUST_TZDIR` point it
  elsewhere.
- **Columnar tables from v0.3** (`USING pgrcolumnar`) are refused with an
  error saying the table is in the v0.3.x columnar format. Dump them with the
  v0.3 binary (`pg_dump`) and restore them into v0.4-beta.

## Status

We don't recommend running pgrust in production (yet), but we are
successfully running it ourselves internally. Keep Postgres as the source
of truth for data you can't afford to lose.

pgrust still has a lot of bugs. Our #1 priority right now is testing and
reliability.

If you need production ready Postgres today, use Postgres.

PostgreSQL extensions don't work out of the box: there is no stable
extension ABI in pgrust yet. But pgrust ships a large number of them,
including pgvector, pg_cron, pg_stat_statements, pg_trgm, hstore, pgcrypto,
postgres_fdw and most of contrib. PL/Python, PL/Perl and PL/Tcl are not
supported yet.

## Performance

Measured on `c8g.4xlarge` (AWS Graviton4), pgrust with pgrcolumnar, its
builtin columnar layout, runs ClickBench's analytical queries up to 1,600x
faster than PostgreSQL (per query, cold runs, against PostgreSQL's published
results on the same instance type).

For a code-level walkthrough of one part of that speedup, read
[how batching, operator fusion, and SIMD speed up the query engine](https://malisper.me/how-we-made-postgres-hundreds-of-times-faster-the-query-engine/).

## Writing

- [How AI Changes the Economics of JIT Compilers](https://malisper.me/how-ai-changes-the-economics-of-jit-compilers/):
  building a copy-and-patch ARM64 JIT in Rust.
- [pgrust: Rebuilding Postgres in Rust with AI](https://malisper.me/pgrust-rebuilding-postgres-in-rust-with-ai/):
  why we started the project.

## Testing

The most common question we get about pgrust is: how can anyone trust it?
Passing a test suite doesn't mean our code is correct.
Getting to the point where people can trust pgrust is our number one priority
today.

To achieve that goal, we're taking several different approaches:

1. Of the 3,400 user facing Postgres functions, we've formally verified
   that 1,397 have identical behavior in pgrust with
   [Kani](https://github.com/model-checking/kani); 466 more are tested
   against Postgres. The ledger is
   [`proofs/USER_FACING_FUNCTIONS.tsv`](proofs/USER_FACING_FUNCTIONS.tsv).
2. We're engaging with [Antithesis](https://antithesis.com) to do simulation
   testing of pgrust to battle test pgrust.
3. We're doing aggressive differential fuzz testing to ensure pgrust's
   behavior is identical to Postgres's.

## Unsafe Code

pgrust uses unsafe code, but only for the specific things that need it.
Postgres represents every internal value as a Datum, an untyped 8 byte
value, and Rust has no safe equivalent, so the code that packs and unpacks
internal values is unsafe. The same goes for the places where pgrust must
match Postgres' memory layouts byte for byte.

If there are particular unsafes that are not necessary and removing them
would not have an impact on performance, let us know, as we would love to
remove more unsafes.

## Building from source

You need the Rust toolchain (any [rustup](https://rustup.rs) install works;
`rust-toolchain.toml` pins the build to Rust 1.96.0 and rustup fetches it
automatically) and the RE2 regex library:

- Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config libre2-dev`
- macOS: `brew install re2 pkg-config`

```bash
cargo build --release --locked -p main_main -p initdb
```

`select version()` names the build: a build in a git checkout prints its short
commit (`PostgreSQL 18.6 (pgrust 0.4-beta, build 1a2b3c4) on ...`); set
`PGRUST_BUILD_ID` at build time to choose the id, or build outside git for none.
`postgres --version` prints `pgrust 0.4-beta (PostgreSQL 18.6 compatible)`;
`postgres -V` prints `postgres (PostgreSQL) 18.6`, the line PostgreSQL's own
`pg_ctl`, `initdb` and `pg_upgrade` check.

The server binary lands at `target/release/postgres`, pgrust's `initdb` beside
it, and the share tree it needs (`postgres.bki`, the setup SQL, `timezone`,
`timezonesets`, tsearch data, extension files) is staged at `target/release/share/`. No C
PostgreSQL is involved in creating or running a cluster:

```bash
target/release/initdb -D /tmp/pgrust-data --no-locale --encoding UTF8 -U postgres
ulimit -s 65520
RUST_MIN_STACK=33554432 target/release/postgres -D /tmp/pgrust-data \
  -k /tmp -p 5432 -c listen_addresses= -c io_method=sync -c max_stack_depth=60000
```

The time zone database is PostgreSQL 18.6's own compiled tzdata, read from
`share/timezone` beside the binary (never the host `zoneinfo`, like C built
without `--with-system-tzdata`). To use the system zoneinfo instead, build with
`PGRUST_SYSTEM_TZDATA=/usr/share/zoneinfo` (C's `--with-system-tzdata`);
`PGRUST_TZDIR` and `PGRUST_PGSHAREDIR` remain runtime overrides, not
requirements. A data directory made
by stock PostgreSQL 18 `initdb` still works too (same on-disk format).
Release builds refuse to compile without RE2 on purpose: a
build with only the fallback regex engine is drastically slower on regex
heavy workloads. The binaries we publish additionally use `--profile dist`,
which turns on fat LTO; it produces a faster binary but takes much longer to
compile.

## What's new in v0.4-beta

- **Gravity, a new query engine.** Gravity runs every query and every kind
  of statement (DML with ON CONFLICT and RETURNING, triggers, row locks,
  cursors, PL/pgSQL and SPI, COPY) with PostgreSQL's semantics, on columnar
  tables and on the ordinary row store alike. It replaces our previous
  engine and runs analytical queries as much as 3x faster than ClickHouse. Its JIT
  was rewritten around a new low-level IR: it compiles each plan to AArch64
  or x86-64 machine code, and to WebAssembly in the browser build, or
  interprets it when compiling would not pay off.
- **pgrcolumnar grows up.** `pgrcolumnar` stores compressed, immutable parts
  with zone maps, delete vectors and background compaction. Reads see
  PostgreSQL MVCC snapshots, and writes are transactional: they roll back
  with the transaction. Small inserts land in a row-store front that is
  folded into columnar parts in the background, and UPDATE and DELETE mark
  rows in delete vectors instead of rewriting parts (ON CONFLICT and MERGE
  are not supported on columnar tables yet). Columnar tables take
  non-unique B-tree, hash, GiST, SP-GiST and GIN indexes, are written to
  WAL, so they survive crashes and replicate to standbys, and support row
  locks and a `sorted_by` table option.
- **One memory budget** covers the buffer pool, the columnar caches and
  running queries. Near the memory limit pgrust cancels the statement holding
  the most memory instead of letting the OS kill the server.
- **jsonb statistics.** `ANALYZE` collects statistics on the keys and values
  inside `jsonb` columns, and the planner uses them for `->`, `->>`, `#>`,
  `#>>` and `?`, `?|`, `?&`, so it estimates jsonb filters instead of
  guessing. On by default (`pgrust.jsonb_path_stats`).
- **The condition cache.** Filter results on columnar tables are reused
  across statements over the same immutable data. `full` is the default
  (also spelled `on`) and stores match counts too. `rows` keeps row
  selections and per-dictionary-code filter tables without counts;
  `granule` keeps only empty-granule verdicts; `off` disables predicate
  reuse. `pgrust.dict_filter_cache` and `pgrust.zone_store` turn off the
  per-dictionary-code filter tables and the zone-map result store on their
  own. Sizing feedback, data caches, and startup prewarm have separate
  controls.
- **pgrust's own `initdb`**, and `pg_cron` 1.6 is included.
- **Upgrading:** columnar tables from v0.3 must be dumped and restored. UTF8 is
  the only server encoding.

v0.4-beta is a beta: it shows what is coming in v0.4 while we finish
stabilizing the rest.

## Developing in the open

Up to v0.3 we developed pgrust privately and published it in large monthly
releases. Starting with v0.4-beta, development happens in this repository:
features, optimizations and bug fixes are pushed here as soon as they are
ready, instead of being held back for the next release.

## Implementation

**Executor**

- Gravity, a vectorized, push-based executor that compiles plans to machine
  code (AArch64 and x86-64) with a JIT that emits code directly.

**Parallelism**

- Threads instead of processes, for both connections and parallel query.
- A query scheduler, new to Postgres. Queries get a priority, and
  long-running queries have theirs lowered, so heavy queries interfere less
  with fast ones.
- Parallel query rebuilt around work stealing: idle threads are assigned
  dynamically to speed up queries already in flight.

**Storage**

- `pgrcolumnar`, a column-oriented format with dictionary encoding and
  several other compression schemes, WAL-logged.
- Pipelined `fsync`. A worker releases its locks after calling `fsync` but
  before it completes. This is safe because the query is not acknowledged,
  and none of its effects are observable, until the `fsync` finishes.

**Other**

- The automatic memory manager. Near the machine's memory limit, pgrust
  cancels the statement holding the most memory, so that one query dies and
  the server itself can keep running.

## Roadmap

Next we're working on testing and battle testing pgrust and making it so
people can trust pgrust with their data.

Beyond that we want to add:

- Instant forking
- Autoscaling including scale to zero
- Planner support for JSON
- Undo log support for a no-vacuum design
- Adaptive planner to prevent bad plans
- A mini version of pgrust designed for testing and being embedded

## Contributing

We are not actively accepting pull requests right now. If you want to help
out with the project, reach out on [Discord](https://discord.gg/FZZ4dbdvwU).

Please do still open an issue if something breaks, if setup is confusing, or
if there is a Postgres behavior you want matched.

Fast, disk space efficient package manager:

* **Fast.** Up to 2x faster than the alternatives (see [benchmark](#benchmark)).
* **Efficient.** Files inside `node_modules` are linked from a single content-addressable storage.
* **[Great for monorepos](https://pnpm.io/workspaces).**
* **Strict.** A package can access only dependencies that are specified in its `package.json`.
* **Deterministic.** Has a lockfile called `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
* **Works as a Node.js version manager.** See [pnpm runtime](https://pnpm.io/11.x/cli/runtime).
* **Works everywhere.** Supports Windows, Linux, and macOS.
* **Battle-tested.** Used in production by teams of [all sizes](https://pnpm.io/workspaces#usage-examples) since 2016.
* **Experimental Rust port.** Includes [pacquet](./pnpm), an experimental port of the CLI written in Rust.
* [See the full feature comparison with npm and Yarn](https://pnpm.io/feature-comparison).

To quote the [Rush](https://rushjs.io/) team:

> Microsoft uses pnpm in Rush repos with hundreds of projects and hundreds of PRs per day, and we've found it to be very fast and reliable.

## Background

pnpm uses a content-addressable filesystem to store all files from all module directories on a disk.
When using npm, if you have 100 projects using lodash, you will have 100 copies of lodash on disk.
With pnpm, lodash will be stored in a content-addressable storage, so:

1. If you depend on different versions of lodash, only the files that differ are added to the store.
  If lodash has 100 files, and a new version has a change only in one of those files,
  `pnpm update` will only add 1 new file to the storage.
1. All the files are saved in a single place on the disk. When packages are installed, their files are linked
  from that single place consuming no additional disk space. Linking is performed using either hard-links or reflinks (copy-on-write).

As a result, you save gigabytes of space on your disk and you have a lot faster installations.
If you'd like more details about the unique `node_modules` structure that pnpm creates and
why it works fine with the Node.js ecosystem, read this small article: [Flat node_modules is not the only way](https://pnpm.io/blog/2020/05/27/flat-node-modules-is-not-the-only-way).

pbakaus/impeccable

The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.

Language: Rust

Stars: 112,176

Forks: 6,693

Stars today: 748 stars today

README

# Impeccable

The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships.

From your project root:

```bash
npx impeccable install
```

Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex).

Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs).

| Without Impeccable | With Impeccable |
|---|---|
| ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) |

Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

## Why

Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.
- **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).
- **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

```
/impeccable critique the pricing cards
```

## How it works

Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context).

Then name a command and a target:

```
/impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout
```

Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut.

### 24 commands

| | Commands |
|---|---|
| **Steer** | `bolder` amplifies safe designs · `quieter` tones down loud ones · `distill` removes what the page doesn't need · `colorize` brings color to a gray interface · `typeset` fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · `layout` fixes spacing and rhythm · `animate` adds transitions and interaction feedback · `delight` adds personality · `overdrive` goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects |
| **Review** | `critique` is a scored UX review · `audit` is a technical quality report |
| **Finish** | `polish` is the final pass before shipping · `harden` covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · `clarify` rewrites unclear copy · `adapt` handles screen sizes and devices · `optimize` fixes loading and rendering performance · `onboard` designs first-run flows and empty states |
| **Iterate live** | `live` lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · `generate` produces variants of a named element without manual picking |
| **Plan and set up** | `shape` plans UX before code · `init` writes `PRODUCT.md` · `document` writes `DESIGN.md` · `extract` pulls repeated patterns into your design system |

The 24th, `craft`, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type `/impeccable` alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs).

On Codex, open `/skills` or type `$impeccable` instead of the slash command.

### Live mode

`/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live).

Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo.

Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the `codex` CLI from your PATH instead (or `claude` when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set `IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat` in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or `off` to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup.

## Three ways to run the detector

**In your agent.** The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. [Automatic design checks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks).

**In CI or your terminal.** The CLI needs no agent:

```bash
npx impeccable detect src/                   # scan a directory
npx impeccable detect https://example.com    # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge)
npx impeccable detect --json .               # machine-readable output
npx impeccable detect --github src/          # GitHub Actions annotations
npx impeccable detect --list-rules           # every rule with its id and description
```

Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: `npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173`.

Exit code `2` means findings, `1` means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run `npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"`. To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: `<!-- impeccable-disable overused-font: exported brand doc -->`. [Run a detector scan](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector) · [Configuration and ignores](https://impeccable.style/docs/config).

**In your browser.** The [Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/impeccable/bdkgmiklpdmaojlpflclinlofgjfpabf) overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. [Review with a visual overlay](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/critique-with-overlay).

## Installation

```bash
npx impeccable install
```

The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`.

Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness).

Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.

<details>
<summary><b>Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins</b></summary>

**Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable.

**GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md).

**Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team)</b></summary>

```bash
git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor
```

Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Manual copy, no Node required</b></summary>

Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder.

| Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` |
| Cursor | `.cursor/` | |
| Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` |
| Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` |
| GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | |
| Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | |
| Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` |
| OpenCode | `.opencode/` | |
| Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` |
| Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` |
| DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` |
| Pi | `.pi/` | |
| Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` |
| Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` |
| Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` |
| Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` |
| Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` |

For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`.

Notes:
- A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path.
- OpenCode also needs `.opencode/commands/impeccable.md` copied into your project's `.opencode/commands/` to provide `/impeccable`.
- Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run `hermes skills trust` from the project root. Global installs need no trust step.
- Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills) and [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) skills docs.
- Restart Trae after copying.
- `impeccable install` and `update` manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when `DSH_HOME` is inside your home directory.

</details>

## Project files and git

Impeccable writes its working files under `.impeccable/`. A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: `config.json`, `live/config.json`, `design.json`, `surfaces/*.md`, and `critique/*.md`. Keep `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.

<details>
<summary><b>Copy the <code>.gitignore</code> entries</b></summary>

```gitignore
# impeccable-ignore-start
# Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides.
# The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace.
# Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json,
# design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md.
**/.impeccable/config.local.json
**/.impeccable/hook.cache.json
**/.impeccable/hook.pending.json
**/.impeccable/*.png
**/.impeccable/review/
**/.impeccable/questions/
**/.impeccable/live/server.json
**/.impeccable/live/sessions/
**/.impeccable/live/previews/
**/.impeccable/live/annotations/
**/.impeccable/live/cache/
**/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-apply-transaction.json
**/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-events.jsonl
**/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-evidence/
**/.impeccable/live/pending-manual-edits.json
**/.impeccable/live/deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json
**/.impeccable/live/*.png
# impeccable-ignore-end
```

</details>

The folders that hold decision-round state (`.impeccable/questions/`, `.impeccable/mocks/worlds/`) also ignore themselves. A `.gitignore` can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run `git rm --cached <path>`.

## Good to know

**Build path.** For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. `init` asks once and saves the answer as `buildPath` in `.impeccable/config.json`; the decision page lets you override it for one session. The choice only appears when your harness can generate images. [Image generation](https://impeccable.style/docs/image-generation) · [Configuration](https://impeccable.style/docs/config).

**Native apps.** Set `## Platform` in `PRODUCT.md` to `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive` (one Flutter or React Native codebase that follows each OS), and the design commands work from Apple's HIG or Material 3 instead of web conventions. `init` asks when it can't tell. `audit` and `adapt` switch to native versions, and the native audit reads SwiftUI, Compose, React Native, or Flutter source directly. The detector, live mode with its `generate` shortcut, and the edit hook stay web-only, because they work on HTML and CSS in a browser.

**Hooks run outside model approval.** In Claude Code, installed command hooks run even when you deny the model's own commands, so the first edit can download the engine. Review installed hooks before unattended runs, or pass `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'` to turn them off for a run. The installer leaves hook entries it didn't add alone.

**Something broken?** `/impeccable doctor` finds stale context files, unused settings, and broken hooks. [Fix setup problems](https://impeccable.style/docs/doctor).

**Telemetry.** When a new design starts, the skill fetches a set of visual directions from the impeccable.style catalog. Turning telemetry off doesn't stop that request; it stops the anonymous record of which directions were shown and which one you picked, which is how the catalog learns what works. Your project name, files, code, and `PRODUCT.md` are never sent. Disable telemetry with `npx impeccable telemetry off`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, or `"telemetry": false` in `.impeccable/config.json` for the whole project. The full list of what is sent is on the [privacy page](https://impeccable.style/privacy).

- **API 服务**：统一由宿主内的 Rust 引擎运行，支持 Responses HTTP/SSE/WebSocket、上下文压缩及 Chat Completions、Claude、Gemini、Ollama 协议兼容。旧 Go/legacy 选择自动迁移，保留账号池、代理、设置、端口、API Key 与历史记录；实例网关继续按 profile 隔离。已移除 Go 引擎和切换入口，不再依赖 Go 工具链或 sidecar。
- **请求身份对照**：Rust 的请求记录「详情」可对照客户端原始 `Session-Id`、`Thread-Id`，以及每次上游尝试使用的请求头、账号和传输方式。关闭或清除正文快照仍保留这些本地诊断信息；客户端未提供与历史未采集分别显示，不按当前配置补填旧记录。这些头值不代表上游已接收请求。

## 安全性与隐私（简明版）

下面是最关心的几个问题，尽量用直白语言说明：

- **这是本地桌面工具**：不需要单独注册平台账号，也不依赖项目自建云端来存你的账号列表。
- **数据主要保存在本机**：
  - `~/.cockpit_tools`：各平台账号、公共配置、日志、备份与实例配置；开发环境使用 `~/.cockpit_tools_dev`，`COCKPIT_TOOLS_DATA_DIR` 可指定自定义目录
  - 已有安装会在后台自动为 `~/.antigravity_cockpit` / `~/.antigravity_cockpit_dev` 建立新名称的兼容入口（Unix 符号链接 / Windows 目录联接），无需手动迁移。旧物理目录和已有实例路径保留，两入口读写同一数据；当前会话保持原路径，后续启动使用新入口。无法建立链接时继续使用旧目录；新旧均为独立目录时保留旧目录，不自动合并或覆盖
  - 受管实例默认位于公共目录的 `instances/<平台>`；Windows 部分平台的实例位于 `%APPDATA%\.cockpit_tools\instances\<平台>`，其旧目录同样自动兼容；自定义目录保持原样
  - `~/.codex`：Codex 官方当前登录 `auth.json`
  - `~/.grok`：Grok CLI 官方默认实例与当前登录 `auth.json`
  - `~/.zcode/v2`：ZCode 官方当前登录加密凭据与配额缓存
  - 已保存的 2FA 及查询历史在应用数据目录的 `mfa_vault.sqlite` 中加密保存，APIKEY.FUN 保存的密钥写入加密文件 `apikey_fun_vault.json`。加密材料保存在应用数据目录中的私有密钥文件，旧 WebView 数据在迁移期间保留。
  - 系统应用数据目录下 `com.jlcodes.cockpit-tools`：宿主应用的 WebView 状态等；历史 `com.antigravity.cockpit-tools` 目录仅用于旧数据兼容导入
- **Grok CLI 凭据不加密**：access token/refresh token 以明文 JSON 保存在本机，主要依赖操作系统账号隔离与本地文件权限保护；Unix 系统上凭据目录设为 `0700`、凭据文件设为 `0600`。脱敏导出不包含 token，不能作为登录备份
- **WebSocket 默认仅本机访问**：监听 `127.0.0.1`，默认端口 `19528`，可在设置中关闭或改端口。
- **什么时候会联网**：OAuth 登录、Token 刷新、配额查询、版本更新检查等官方接口请求。
- **macOS 隐私权限弹窗说明**：在 Cockpit Tools 中启动 Codex/agent 后，如果 agent 执行的 shell 命令访问桌面、文稿、下载、照片等受保护目录，macOS 可能会把权限请求显示为“Cockpit Tools 想要访问……”。这是因为这些命令是 Cockpit Tools 启动的子进程，系统会把权限归因到宿主应用；这不等同于 Cockpit Tools 主程序主动扫描这些目录。是否允许取决于你是否信任当前 agent 任务和它将要执行的命令；不确定时可以选择拒绝，或先把项目放在普通工作目录中运行。
- **实用安全建议**：
  1. 不使用插件联动时，可关闭 WebSocket 服务。
  2. 不要把用户目录直接打包分享；备份前注意脱敏 token 文件。
  3. 在公共或共用电脑上，使用后删除账号并退出应用。

### WebSocket 账号切换 API

`request.switch_account` 支持明确选择 Antigravity 客户端。未传 `runtime_target`，或传 `"antigravity_ide"`，选择 IDE。IDE 2.6 起使用共享凭据，启用切号启动时通过重启加载新账号。旧版 IDE 继续使用现有启动和无感切号设置。

切换 Antigravity 桌面版及使用同一系统凭据的 `agy` CLI，可发送：

```json
{"type":"request.switch_account","payload":{"account_id":"<account-id>","request_id":"x","runtime_target":"antigravity","launch_on_switch":false}}
```

- `runtime_target: "antigravity"`：复用桌面版切号认证规则；2.0 及以上版本写入系统凭据，并同步桌面版的本地回退文件 `~/.gemini/jetski-standalone-oauth-token`，并同步已初始化的 `agy` 会话。凭据文件保留 `id_token`，Unix 权限为 `0600`。旧版桌面 App 写入本地 SQLite 登录状态。只有真实凭据及回退文件写入成功后才更新当前账号、默认实例绑定并通知切号结果。回退文件同步失败会明确报告系统凭据已写入并提示重试。
- `launch_on_switch`：仅用于 `"antigravity"`，默认 `false`；不关闭或启动客户端，已运行桌面版可能需下次启动才使用新账号。显式传 `true` 才执行与桌面版 UI 相同的关闭、写入、重启流程。IDE 请求不要传此字段，继续使用现有设置。
- `request_id`：可选，传入后返回对应的 `response.success` 或 `response.error`。不支持的目标、凭据写入失败或并发桌面切号会返回错误，不报告成功；凭据已切换但启动失败会明确报告启动错误。无效目标返回 `WS_SWITCH_TARGET_INVALID`，在 IDE 请求中传启动策略返回 `WS_SWITCH_LAUNCH_POLICY_INVALID`；并发桌面切号返回 `ANTIGRAVITY_SWITCH_BUSY`，账号准备超时返回 `ANTIGRAVITY_SWITCH_PREPARATION_TIMEOUT`。
- `ANTIGRAVITY_SWITCH_STATE_SAVE_FAILED` 表示客户端凭据已切换，但 Tools 当前账号状态保存失败，请重试切号。共享登录会同步保存两端的默认账号绑定。

## 安装指南 (Installation)

### 选项 A: 手动下载 (推荐)

前往 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/jlcodes99/cockpit-tools/releases) 下载对应系统的安装包：

*   **macOS**: `.dmg` (Apple Silicon & Intel)
*   **Windows**: `.msi`（推荐）、`.exe`，或 `x64-portable.zip`（解压即用，无需安装）

Windows 便携包解压后直接运行其中的 `Cockpit Tools.exe`（或同名主程序）。系统需要 Windows 10/11 的 Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime；账号和配置仍按当前 Windows 用户目录保存，不会随 ZIP 文件夹自动迁移。
*   **Linux**: `.deb` (Debian/Ubuntu)、`.rpm` 或 `.AppImage` (通用)

### 选项 B: Homebrew 安装 (macOS)

> 需要先安装 Homebrew。

```bash
brew tap jlcodes99/cockpit-tools https://github.com/jlcodes99/cockpit-tools
brew install --cask cockpit-tools
```

macOS 正式包的发布流程要求 Apple Developer ID 签名与公证；正常安装无需添加 `--no-quarantine`。历史未签名版本不会因流程更新而自动获得签名。

如果提示已存在应用（例如：`already an App at '/Applications/Cockpit Tools.app'`），请先删除旧版本再安装：

```bash
rm -rf "/Applications/Cockpit Tools.app"
brew install --cask cockpit-tools
```

或者直接强制覆盖安装：

```bash
brew install --cask --force cockpit-tools
```

### 🛠️ 常见问题排查 (Troubleshooting)

#### Windows：Codex 反复提示“Windows 设置未完成”？

若当前错误为 `helper_sandbox_lock_failed` 且 `.sandbox-bin` 目录访问被拒绝，请参阅[Codex Windows 沙箱临时恢复说明](docs/codex-windows-sandbox-recovery.md)。该问题已在 Codex 上游报告；恢复工具默认只读，需手动修复并保留回滚备份。

ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve

Fast and lightweight DB Client made in Rust and GPUI.

Language: Rust

Stars: 1,548

Forks: 88

Stars today: 59 stars today

README

# <img src="assets/icon/dbdelve.svg" alt="" width="48" align="absmiddle"> DBDelve

A fast, native, cross-platform, multi-engine database client. Written in Rust
with GPUI, no Electron and no JVM: instant startup, friendly on your memory,
and smooth scrolling through large tables where other clients crash or
introduce limits.


## Community

Ideas and discussion on [Discord](https://discord.gg/7PegWzwqCm).


![DBDelve in Gruvbox Dark Glass: a SELECT on the events table in the editor and its result grid below](assets/screenshots/query-dark.png)

![DBDelve in Gruvbox Light Glass: a join in the editor and its result grid below](assets/screenshots/query-light.png)

Scrolling a million rows:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e15d566-a110-46c6-a236-52af7d877d4c

Launching, with the last results already there:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e55da56-8577-43e0-812a-c77eb5d0e701

## Why

I wanted something which is performant, modern and consumes little ram. The existing DB clients are either filled with bloat (Electron and JVM) or paid. This is an alternative to them. No feature is ever going behind a paywall and with time we will have complete parity on features with those too.

## Install

**macOS** (Apple Silicon, macOS 12 or later):

```sh
brew install --cask ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/dbdelve
```

The app isn't notarized, so the cask clears the quarantine flag macOS would
otherwise refuse it over. Without Homebrew:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/main/install.sh | sh
```

**Linux** (x86_64 or aarch64): the same one-liner installs it under `~/.local`
with no root, or `yay -S dbdelve-bin` from the AUR, or the tarball or AppImage
from [the latest release][releases].

**Windows** (x86_64): run the installer from [the latest release][releases],
or unzip the zip and run `dbdelve.exe`. The installer asks for AppData (just
for you) or Program Files (all users).

Updating, the `.dmg`, Linux requirements, building from source and where your
data lives are all in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md).

[releases]: https://github.com/ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/releases/latest

## Supported databases

Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Turso, DuckDB, Snowflake, SQL Server, MongoDB,
Redis (and Valkey, KeyDB, Dragonfly) and ClickHouse.

Any other database with an ODBC driver is reachable through the bundled ODBC
bridge, with that driver installed: IBM Db2, Oracle, SAP HANA, SAP ASE
(Sybase), Informix, Teradata, Vertica, Exasol, Firebird, Amazon Redshift,
Google BigQuery, Databricks, Apache Hive, Trino and Presto, Dremio,
InterSystems IRIS, Microsoft Access and more. See
[Connecting through ODBC](docs/odbc.md).


![The welcome screen: paste a connection URL or pick one of the engines, import from DBeaver or TablePlus, or pick a theme](assets/screenshots/welcome.png)

## What it does

- **Make it yours.** The app's own themes alongside Catppuccin, Tokyo Night,
  Gruvbox and Dracula, each in dark, light and glass. Import themes from Zed or
  VS Code, or [write your own](docs/themes.md).

  ![The theme picker, with themes imported from Zed and VS Code and the import commands below them](assets/screenshots/themes.png)

- **Bring your connections with you.** Import every saved connection,
  passwords and SSH settings included, from DBeaver, or TablePlus on macOS.
- **Organize your connections into projects,** and jump to any of them from
  the palette, or disconnect back to a home screen that lists them all.

  ![The palette scoped to connections, grouped into two projects, with the current connection marked](assets/screenshots/projects.png)

- **Never mistake prod for staging.** Every connection is isolated and can
  color the title bar. Run it read-only, read-write or with full access, and
  DBDelve asks before anything destructive.

  ![The connection form, grouped into connection, security and behaviour, with a color and a project for the connection](assets/screenshots/connection-form.png)

- **Edits you can read first.** Change a cell and DBDelve writes the `UPDATE`
  for you to check before it runs.
- **Keep the columns you need.** Hide or pin columns, and the layout survives
  a restart.
- **Read a row in full** in the row panel, with JSON highlighted, and edit long
  values there.

  ![A table open in the grid, with the row panel showing one row's values and its JSON highlighted](assets/screenshots/table-dark.png)

- **Import rows** from CSV, TSV or JSON, with every row checked and every
  statement shown before anything runs.

  ![Importing events.csv: format options on the left, each file column mapped to a table column, and a preview of the rows](assets/screenshots/import.png)

- **Open a data file** by dropping it on the window: a CSV, Excel, Parquet or
  JSON file opens in DuckDB, held in memory, as a query you can change. A
  `.sql` file opens in a new query tab on the connection you're on, and runs
  only when you run it.

- **See the query plan** highlighted in its own pane, with bad row estimates
  called out.

  ![An Explain Analyze plan for a join: each node with its actual and estimated rows and time, and a ×76 misestimate flagged](assets/screenshots/query-plan.png)

- **Completion that knows your schema:** tables, and a table's columns after
  its name and a dot. A table is written with an alias, and after `JOIN` with
  the condition its foreign keys imply.

  ![Completing accounts. to its columns in a join](assets/screenshots/completion.png)

- **Keyboard-first.** One palette for commands, tables, saved queries, history
  and connections, and every shortcut rebindable.

  <img src="assets/screenshots/shortcuts.png" width="360" alt="The Shortcuts page in Settings: every action with its key binding and an Edit button">

- **Your SSH, not a reimplementation.** Tunnels run through your own `ssh`, so
  your config, agent and hardware keys just work.
  For Postgres, a Host that is a directory (`/var/run/postgresql`) reaches that
  Unix socket on the SSH host, optionally as another user (Run as); the server
  needs `socat`, and passwordless `sudo` for it when Run as is set. TLS modes
  other than `disable` and `prefer` are refused there.
- **Reach private databases through AWS SSM.** Choose AWS SSM in the connection
  form to use your installed AWS CLI and Session Manager plugin, with profile
  and region settings and automatic local port selection. See
  [SSM tunnels](docs/ssm-tunnels.md) for setup and TLS restrictions.
- **Sign in with a short-lived token.** On Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL
  Server, Redis and ClickHouse, a profile's Password command prints the
  password at every login, so cloud IAM auth keeps working after the token
  expires. For Amazon RDS:

  ```sh
  /opt/homebrew/bin/aws rds generate-db-auth-token --hostname %HOSTNAME% --port %PORT% --username %USERNAME% --region <region>
  ```

  `%HOSTNAME%`, `%PORT%` and `%USERNAME%` are the profile's own. DBDelve
  quotes them itself, so write them unquoted: one inside quotes stops the
  command from running. Give the program's full path (`which aws` prints it):
  an app opened from the Finder or a desktop launcher does not see the PATH
  your shell sets. Expires after
  reuses the output for that many seconds, in memory only; blank runs the
  command at every login.

Free and open source, nothing behind a paywall, and no telemetry: the only
request DBDelve makes on its own is an update check, which you can turn off.

## Benchmarks

DBDelve 0.3.6 against DBeaver 25.3.1 on the same Postgres table, median of 5
runs each (2026-10-11, M1 Pro, 32 GB):

|                   | DBDelve | DBeaver |
| ----------------- | ------- | ------- |
| Launch            | 1.1 s   | 5.2 s   |
| Idle memory       | 133 MB  | 606 MB  |
| 1,000-row query   | 0.21 s  | 1.96 s  |
| 1M rows, time     | 56 s    | 208 s   |
| 1M rows, memory\* | 4.9 GB  | 17 GB   |

\* The whole 1M-row table pulled into memory on purpose, with the row limit
off. Method and full results in [BENCHMARKS.md](BENCHMARKS.md).

## Logs and bug reports

DBDelve keeps a diagnostic log on your machine and never sends it anywhere. To
attach it to an issue, use **Help → Copy Diagnostics** and paste; **Help → Open
Logs Folder** shows the files. If the default log doesn't show the problem, turn
on **Verbose logging** in Settings and reproduce it.

Read a log before you post it and remove anything sensitive. A verbose one can
hold hostnames, database names and anything a database driver logs.

[GPL-3.0](LICENSE). Code contributed before the switch was released under the
[MIT License](licenses/MIT-dbdelve.txt), and that notice still applies to it.
Third-party font and theme licenses are in [NOTICES.md](NOTICES.md).

## Sponsors

Support DBDelve on [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/membership/30003257). Sponsors are listed here and on the site.

<a href="https://dbdelve.github.io/#sponsors"><img src="https://dbdelve.github.io/sponsors/sponsors.svg" alt="DBDelve's sponsors"></a>

## Contributors

Thank you to everyone who has contributed to DBDelve.

<a href="https://github.com/ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/graphs/contributors"><img src="https://contrib.rocks/image?repo=ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve" alt="DBDelve's contributors"></a>

Want to join them? Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

Agent2API is an **AI routing gateway with Agent client takeover**. It exposes a unified model API for custom AI providers and centralizes account routing, model mapping, gateway keys and request reports. It also manages local Agent clients' connection profiles, including importing, switching and previewing configuration changes.

## ✨ Key Features

- 🔌 **Unified model APIs** — OpenAI Chat / Responses / Images and Anthropic Messages, with a unified model catalog; Raccoon, Loomy, Antigravity, ModelScope, WorkBuddy and Doubao Work supply image generation, while Raccoon, Loomy, Antigravity, ModelScope and WorkBuddy also support reference-image editing. Both are available as AI assistant tools
- 🧭 **AI routing** — model mapping, account priority, load balancing, session affinity and failover in one place
- 🤖 **Agent client takeover** — manage multiple connection profiles for local clients, import existing settings, preview writes and switch between the gateway and custom services
- 🧩 **Plugin extensions** — additional provider implementations are installed and updated separately, not bundled with the application; custom providers do not require them
- 🛡️ **Egress proxies** — select proxy-pool exits for accounts and update tasks
- 🔑 **Gateway security** — scoped gateway keys, optional human verification for panel sign-in, and model requests refused by default until a key is configured
- 📊 **Request reports** — request volume, success rate, token usage, cache hit rate and a 365-day heatmap
- ⏰ **Background maintenance** — model catalog refresh, credential maintenance and software update checks; daily check-in runs per provider on that provider's own window (Qoder 10:01, ZCode 19:01, others follow the schedule time), plus a catch-up round that only touches accounts not yet checked in; additional provider-specific tasks are supplied by plugins
